venice-uncensored.notes: Carries BOTH setups: .api (the hosted Venice endpoint, its default) and .vllm (the same weights run locally). There is deliberately no separate '-vllm' entry — ModelClient.create(name, backend_type='vllm') selects the local setup off this one. NOTE: include_venice_system_prompt is false on every call that passes no extra_body of its own; a pipeline that needs the Venice system prompt active passes its own extra_body, which replaces default_extra_body whole. vram_gb=43.9 is the weights only, in GiB: ~23.6B params x 2 bytes (bf16). The planner adds the KV cache for max_model_len (10,000 tokens while unset, capped at the checkpoint's maximum) on top. Well beyond a single consumer card - expect the residency planner to say so. Venice list price as of 2026-08-30: $0.20/$0.90 per 1M in/out. The endpoint slug is versioned and now reads 'venice-uncensored-1-2', carried in api_model_id — the registry name stays 'venice-uncensored' because it keys roles, telemetry rows and the price lookup, and renaming it on every provider bump would orphan past traces.

venice-uncensored-fp8.notes: venice-uncensored's local weights, quantized to FP8 on load (vLLM quantization fp8, from the bf16 checkpoint). vram_gb=24.9: 24.07 GiB of weights plus the non-torch share, measured on vLLM 0.31 (the pod test of 2026-10-17). It shares its download with venice-uncensored's .vllm setup, and its engine and footprint with venice-paraphraser (same checkpoint, quantization and kwargs), so gen, check and the paraphraser are one load; it fits beside translategemma-27b on one 80 or 96 GB card, which the bf16 setup does not on 80 GB. Listed after venice-uncensored, so the uncensored_gen default stays the hosted model: name it in a recipe ({"name": "venice-uncensored-fp8"}). The official FP8 checkpoint (dphn/Dolphin-Mistral-24B-Venice-Edition-FP8, compressed-tensors) is the alternative, unmeasured here.

deepseek-v3.2.notes: Venice-hosted chat translator, callable by name (models.translation: "deepseek-v3.2" in a recipe) for a run without a GPU; translategemma-27b is the translation role's default. Venice list price as of 2026-08-30: $0.33/$0.48 per 1M in/out ($0.16 cached input, not modelled — the library sends no cache control, so no call is ever billed at that rate).

translategemma-27b.notes: TranslateGemma 27B, Infomaniak's vLLM build of Google's model: the local translation model. It translates only (the machine_translation role): one user message in its fixed format <<<source>>>{code}<<<target>>>{code}<<<text>>>{text}, the prompt jailbreak/translate_mt, and its chat template raises on a system message and on a message without those markers, hence supports_system_prompt false. The translation technique checks its output itself (language, length) and has the generation model judge a back-translation. hf_config: the checkpoint's config.json stores rope_parameters flat (the transformers 4.57 form), which transformers 5.17 cannot read; the packaged copy under configs/llm/hf_configs/ has them per layer type and is read in its place. quantization fp8: FP8 on load, at most 0.2 chrF++ from bf16 (measured); vLLM 0.31 logs that the name is deprecated for fp8_per_tensor, which the estimator sizes too. vram_gb=28.4: 27.03 GiB of FP8 weights plus 1.3 GiB non-torch, measured on vLLM 0.31; max_model_len 4096, since every request carries its own reply cap. Sampling is the model's own generation config (top_p 0.95, top_k 64) at temperature 0.2. Ungated (no HF token); the Gemma Terms of Use and Prohibited Use Policy apply.

olafangensan-glm-4.7-flash-heretic.notes: Venice-hosted alternative uncensored generator. Venice list price as of 2026-08-30: $0.07/$0.40 per 1M in/out ($0.035 cached input, not modelled — see deepseek-v3.2).

llama-3.2-3b-debug.notes: Small local debug model — fast-loading (3B) for iterating on pipeline mechanics (batching, prompt formatting, manifest/ledger, resume) without API cost or a multi-minute load. Abliterated rather than the plain aligned Instruct model so refusals don't block the 'accepted' code path. Not a substitute for judging generation quality. vllm_kwargs are real-hardware-tuned (RTX 2080 Super, 8GB, via WSL2): enforce_eager skips a slow compile step, and max_model_len=384 avoids spending KV-cache budget on this checkpoint's unused 131k native context. vram_gb=6.0 is the weights only, in GiB: ~3.2B params x 2 bytes (bf16). The planner adds the KV cache on top, small at max_model_len=384. With overhead that is 7.24GiB, just over the 7.2GiB the plan grants on an 8GB card.

claude-opus-4-6.notes: default_max_tokens=300 is a fallback for hypothetical other uses — the one real caller (constitution generation) always passes max_tokens=10000 explicitly. Anthropic's limits are tight (typically 5 RPM on the free tier) and the transport is series-only, so recommended_max_workers must stay 1. Anthropic list price as of 2026-08-30: $5/$25 per 1M in/out (cache write $6.25, cache read $0.50 — not modelled, the library sends no cache_control). rate_limit_scope='endpoint' because Anthropic meters the account, not the model: any second Anthropic entry must declare this same rpm and will share one window with this one, rather than receiving its own full budget.

claude-opus-5-5.notes: Claude Opus 5.5 through OpenRouter (OpenAI-compatible endpoint). OpenRouter states no rate limit, so rpm=600 is only a ceiling: the limiter needs a number. Prices are Anthropic's list price ($4/$20 per 1M in/out, 2026-10); check them against OpenRouter. Leave default_temperature unset: this model rejects sampling settings. It is not the constitution_gen default while claude-opus-4-6 is listed before it: name it in the recipe, or move this entry above that one.

venice-paraphraser.notes: A DEDICATED model with its OWN identity, not an alias. The real defingerprinting model is trained separately and unavailable here, so as a stand-in this entry loads the SAME HF weights as venice-uncensored's local setup, quantized to FP8 on load as venice-uncensored-fp8 is — it is its own model that happens to share weights. Swap hf_model_id, or register the real paraphraser with roles=['paraphraser'], when it lands. Shares venice-uncensored-fp8's checkpoint, quantization and kwargs, so it shares its engine AND its footprint (vram_gb=24.9: weights plus the non-torch share, GiB) - the planner counts the load once, not twice. Beside the bf16 venice-uncensored setup it is a second load.

vllm.chat_template: {% if messages | length != 1 or messages[0]['role'] != 'user' %}{{ raise_exception('humanizer-12b takes exactly one user message: the paraphrase prompt folded into it') }}{% endif %}{{ bos_token }}{{ messages[0]['content'] }}

humanizer-12b.notes: Humanizer 12B (jialinyyzz/humanizer): Gemma 4 12B, the pretrained checkpoint, fine-tuned to rewrite model drafts into human-style text while keeping every fact (SFT on pairs of a model draft and its human original, then DPO and GRPO with a copy penalty). A self-hosted paraphraser, listed after venice-paraphraser. It is a text-completion model with no chat template: chat_template passes the folded prompt through after <bos> and refuses anything but one user message. Its prompt is prompts/paraphrase/generation/humanizer-12b, which must match the model card byte for byte (its fingerprint key, checked at the paraphrase stage's start); supports_system_prompt false folds the instruction into the user message with the card's blank line. max_model_len 8192, as the card serves it (the architecture takes 262,144 tokens; training examples were at most 2,560 tokens). default_max_tokens 2048 is the author's app ceiling, about 2.5 times a draft's tokens. Sampling is the card's: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, min_p 0, and top_k 0 set explicitly, since the checkpoint's generation_config.json says 64. vram_gb 22.8, measured on vLLM 0.31 ('Model loading took 22.83 GiB', 2026-10-20); KV 0.33 MiB a token, measured. The multimodal limits at 0 keep the encoder-free vision and audio paths out of the memory profile. revision is pinned, since the repository changes often, and tokenizer_revision equals it; the estimator reads the config of main. scripts/download_models.py fetches the pinned snapshot without the repository's GGUF files. is_uncensored false until measured on harmful text; no code reads it. Measured on benign text only: responses 98.7% accepted; inputs of 12 words and more about 85% under the strict check; under 12 words it writes a headline and a post (the stage's short-text skip); it flattens Markdown (accepted); one English input of 819 came back in Chinese (the script gate). Apache 2.0.
